## Design

### 2026-10-10 – #### October 5 - 6: Panduck idea and concept by evellkz

**1h**

#### October 5 - 6: Panduck idea and concept by evellkz

Before touching KiCad, i spent some time figuring out what Panduck actually is.

**The idea (Oct 5):** I want a tiny desk companion that feels alive, not just another gadget. Panduck is a little duck that sits on my desk and shows how my day is going through its face, sounds, lights, and small moves. Happy when a notification comes in, excited on a GitHub commit, focused when i'm in the zone, and a sad X_X face when my build fails.

**Features (Oct 5):** Screen for the face, speaker + mic for sound and voice commands, a rotary knob with push button for control, RGB lights for moods, and some sensors. It connects to my PC over Wi-Fi, so a Python agent can tell it what's happening.

**Look and size (Oct 6):** Designed the cute duck look with the little yellow tuft on top. About 10 x 10 x 11 cm, so it fits on a desk without taking over. Also made the poster to put everything in one place, expressions, hardware breakdown, and tech stack.

**Next:** Turn the idea into a real PCB. Hopefully it quacks :D

### 2026-10-10 – #### October 5 - 7: Panduck schematic (5h progress, actually 3h

**3h**

#### October 5 - 7: Panduck schematic (5h progress, actually 3h

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 144130](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/iLGJiHEs2pHLWDGxKwPYeIkFIYtwq3Qd/543b0ed765f94aa961da3005931816fc01c3cbfb82cabc80d01079450df82693.png)

) by evellkz

Got the whole schematic done in about 5 hours, from picking parts to the last net label.

**Research (Oct 5):** Looked for parts that fit a tiny duck body. Went with ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 (N16R8) for the brain, BQ24074 for USB-C battery charging, TPS63020 buck-boost for 3.3V, MAX98357A for the speaker, and an I2S mic. For sensors: IMU, SHT40, VEML7700 and a fuel gauge. Then downloaded symbols and footprints for everything.

**Schematic (Oct 6-7):** Drew it in KiCad and split it into 6 sections: power, MCU, display, audio, sensors, and UI (LEDs, buttons, encoder). The display only gets a connector (J_DISP) to its own little board, since the panel is still TBD.

**Decision I reversed:** I started with a regular ESP32-WROOM-32, but it was running out of pins with display, knob, speaker, mic and sensors all on it. Switched to the ESP32-S3. More GPIO, native USB, and enough PSRAM for the face animations. Had to redo the MCU section, but worth it.

**Next:** PCB layout and routing.
**Time spent this session: 3 hours**

#### October 8 - 10: Panduck PCB layout + final routing (3h) by evellkz

Finished the PCB!

![panduck_finalroute](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/iLGJiHEs2pHLWDGxKwPYeIkFIYtwq3Qd/7e4ea03148556557b94805f1c7526090e92a6eb8fd96b039591edbcf3b4d90bc.png)

**Layout (Oct 8-9):** Imported the netlist into the PCB editor and it was a mess of ratlines at first, haha. Set the board outline with 4 mounting holes, then placed everything. The ESP32-S3 goes at the edge with a keep-out zone for the antenna. USB-C and the battery connector sit on the bottom edge. The display, encoder and LED parts connect through their own headers (J_DISP, J_ENC, J_LED), so the main board stays small.

**Routing (Oct 10):** Routed the whole board with zero ratlines left! Short traces for SPI, I2S and the LED lines, wider traces for the power and battery paths, and ground pour on the back. Then I ran DRC and fixed the clearance errors.

**What was hard:** Too many parts in a tiny space. I moved parts around a lot just to get a clean path for the I2S lines.

**Next:** 3D printed case, then check the board fits inside.
